newsitem.title: CHINA: Chinese airlines get nod for Pudong facilities.
newsitem.headline: Chinese airlines get nod for Pudong facilities.

text.p: Two Chinese airlines have been given permission to build support facilities at Shanghai's new Pudong airport and an application from Germany's Lufthansa is under consideration, a newspaper report said.
The China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday that work on the first phase of the Pudong airport, 30 km east of the city centre, is due to begin soon with completion scheduled for 1999.
It said China Eastern Airlines and Shanghai Airlines had received approval to begin work on their aircraft and passenger facilities.
It quoted an official as saying that Lufthansa's application, if approved, would make it the first foreign airline to be allowed to service aircraft and make overnight stops at Pudong airport.
"But negotiations haven't been completed," the official added.
No foreign carriers have service bases at Shanghai's existing Hongqiao airport.
